source.title: Representation of confidence associated with a decision by neurons in the parietal cortex

confidence_rationale: Direct single-unit evidence that a graded confidence readout exists and is used in an animal with no linguistic reconstruction stage at all, and that it is read from the state of the generating (evidence-accumulation) dynamics. This supports ARC-116's central separation: the readout does not require, and is not derived from, a verbal reconstruction. Discounted because the same LIP neurons carry both the decision variable and the certainty signal, so the paper argues against a strong anatomical separation of generation and readout, and it says nothing about stage 3.
failure_signatures: The same LIP neurons that represent formation of the direction decision also encode the certainty used for the opt-out choice, so generation and readout share a substrate; a strong reading of 'non-collapsible' as 'anatomically separate' is not supported.
No reconstruction channel exists in the preparation, so the paper cannot test whether degrading reconstruction spares the readout -- it shows only that the readout exists without one.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Rhesus monkeys discriminating random-dot motion could opt out for a small certain reward after stimulus viewing; they did so in a way that tracked their certainty, and neurons in lateral intraparietal cortex represented both formation of the direction decision and the degree of certainty underlying the decision to opt out.
mapping.ree_translation: Stage 2 of ARC-116 (a metacognitive readout) is present, graded and behaviourally consequential in an agent with no stage 3 (verbal reconstruction). The readout is a function of the generating dynamics' own state, not of any post-hoc account of them -- which is the architecture ARC-116 requires and the collapsed alternative (readout derived FROM reconstruction) cannot produce here.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Shows the readout can exist without reconstruction; does not show that it stays independent of reconstruction when one exists (humans). Shared neurons for decision and certainty mean 'non-collapsible' must be read functionally (distinct computations over one substrate), not anatomically. Monkey perceptual decisions, not the 'nonverbal settling' of open-ended thought.
mapping.source_context: Rhesus macaques, random-dot motion direction discrimination with a post-stimulus sure-target (opt-out) option; single-unit LIP recordings.

confidence_components.notes: Canonical Science paper, well replicated in spirit. Mapping moderate: strong on the 'readout without reconstruction' leg, silent on the degradation dissociation the falsifier names.
